overview: Australia is made up of the mainland of the Australian continent, the island of Tasmania and many smaller islands. Its capital is Canberra and its largest city is Sydney. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples have lived in Australia for at least 50,000 years, and their cultures are among the oldest continuing cultures on Earth. British settlement began in 1788, and the separate colonies joined together as one country in 1901.

geography.text: Australia is the driest inhabited continent. Most of the interior, known as the Outback, is desert or dry grassland, and most people live along the coasts, especially in the south-east. The Great Dividing Range runs down the east, and off the north-east coast lies the Great Barrier Reef, the largest coral reef system in the world. Uluru, a huge sandstone rock in the centre, is sacred to its Aboriginal owners.

history.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples have lived in Australia for at least 50,000 years. Britain founded a convict colony at Sydney in 1788, and settlement spread across the continent, devastating Indigenous communities. The six colonies united as the Commonwealth of Australia in 1901. In 1967 Australians voted to include Aboriginal people in the national census, and in 2008 the government formally apologised to the Stolen Generations.

events.title: Cook maps the east coast
events.text: James Cook claims eastern Australia for Britain.

events.title: The First Fleet
events.text: British ships bring convicts to Sydney Cove.

events.title: Gold rush
events.text: Gold is discovered, bringing a rush of immigrants.

events.title: Federation
events.text: Six colonies unite as one country.

events.title: Referendum
events.text: Australians vote to count Aboriginal people in the census.

events.title: National apology
events.text: The government apologises to the Stolen Generations.

government.text: Australia is a federal constitutional monarchy. The British monarch is head of state, represented by a Governor-General, and the Prime Minister leads the government with the support of the House of Representatives. Parliament also has a Senate. Australia has six states and two main territories. Voting is compulsory, and in 1999 Australians voted against becoming a republic.

economy.text: Australia is one of the world's biggest exporters of iron ore, coal, natural gas, gold and lithium, much of it sold to China. It also exports beef, wheat and wool, and international students and tourism bring in a lot of money. Australia went almost 30 years without a recession, from 1991 to 2020.

culture.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples have the oldest continuous cultures on Earth, with art and stories reaching back tens of thousands of years. Australia is famous for its unique animals, such as kangaroos, koalas and platypuses, and for the Great Barrier Reef, the largest coral reef system in the world. The Sydney Opera House is a UNESCO site.

items.title: Sydney Opera House
items.text: Opened in 1973; its roof looks like billowing sails.

items.title: Uluru
items.text: A huge sandstone rock sacred to the Anangu people.

items.title: Great Barrier Reef
items.text: More than 2,900 reefs, visible from space.

sport.text: Australians are mad about sport. Cricket, rugby league, rugby union and Australian rules football, a fast game invented in Melbourne, draw huge crowds. Australia hosted the Summer Olympics in Melbourne in 1956 and Sydney in 2000, and Brisbane hosts in 2032. Swimming has brought it many Olympic golds.

items.text: Melbourne, Sydney and Brisbane: Olympic host cities.

items.title: Australian Open
items.text: One of tennis's four Grand Slams, held in Melbourne every January.

items.title: Cricket World Cup
items.text: Australia's men have won it a record six times.

didYouKnow: Australia is the only country that covers a whole continent.
